notes: Revival; Peter Graves returns as Jim Phelps. Same name as the 1966 series.

in_universe.label: After the 1966–73 series (Phelps called out of retirement)
in_universe.note: After his protégé and successor as leader of the top-secret Impossible Missions Force is killed, Jim Phelps is called out of retirement and asked to form a new IMF team and track down the assassin.

in_universe.label: Contemporary (no year stated)
in_universe.note: In the first film of the series, Ethan Hunt is framed for the murder of his Impossible Mission Force (IMF) team during a botched mission in Prague and accused of selling government secrets to an arms dealer known only as "Max".

release.note: Wikipedia: Mission: Impossible was theatrically released in the United States by Paramount Pictures on May 22, 1996.

links.note: film adaptation of the TV series; Jim Phelps (recast) appears; separate continuity

in_universe.label: Contemporary (no year stated)
in_universe.note: In the second film, Ethan Hunt goes back in action and works with a professional thief Nyah Nordoff-Hall (Thandie Newton).

release.note: Wikipedia: Mission: Impossible 2 was theatrically released in the United States by Paramount Pictures on May 24, 2000, and grossed over $546 million worldwide

title: Mission: Impossible III

in_universe.note: In the third film, Ethan is engaged to Julia Meade (Michelle Monaghan), who is unaware of his true job.

title: Mission: Impossible – Ghost Protocol
notes: Release date is the US theatrical date; the premiere was earlier.

in_universe.label: Contemporary (no year stated)
in_universe.note: In the fourth film, Ethan and the entire IMF are framed for the bombing of the Kremlin while investigating an individual known only as "Cobalt" (Michael Nyqvist).

release.note: Wikipedia: Mission: Impossible – Ghost Protocol premiered at the Dubai International Film Festival on December 7, 2011, and was released in IMAX and select large-format theaters on December 16, before being theatrically released in the United States by Paramount Pictures on December 21.

title: Mission: Impossible – Fallout
notes: Release date is the US theatrical date; the premiere was earlier.

in_universe.label: Two years after Rogue Nation
in_universe.note: Set two years after the events of Rogue Nation, Fallout follows Impossible Missions Force agent Ethan Hunt (Cruise) and his team in their efforts to prevent a nuclear attack by terrorist Solomon Lane (Harris) and the mysterious extremist John Lark.

release.note: Wikipedia: Mission: Impossible – Fallout premiered in Paris on July 12, 2018, and was theatrically released in the United States on July 27.
